title: Holdfast release scratchpad
content:
Purpose / context:
- Working scratchpad for a small-batch, "holdfast" style release flow. Intended for feature flips and model-variant pins where we need conservative warmup + quick pinback.
- Not final — collab notes for SRE/serving/runtime/product to distill into a playbook.

High level idea:
- "Holdfast" = anchor a tiny steady cohort (0.5–2% traffic) that we gradually bind (pin) to the new variant while a broader warmup playlist quietly warms cache/KV and client SDK priming. Maintain an anchored rollback escape hatch (instant pin to prior variant).

Anchors and cohorts:
- Anchor cohorts: pick 3 low-risk clients (internal test tenants, canary customers) + 1 synthetic traffic stream.
- Secondary probe cohort: random 0.5% user traffic from low-QPS clients.
- Quiet cohort: ephemeral SDK toggles for 50 dev seats (to validate UX changes).

Sequence (rough):
1) Preflight (T-24h)
   - Verify model artifact built + checksum (SHA256).
   - Smoke test in staging: 50k tokens across typical prompt families.
   - Upload perf profile to console and attach to rollout ticket.
   - Add feature flag and generate SDK toggles for dev seats.

2) Warmup playlist (T-3h to T+6h)
   - Seed KV/prefix cache using synthetic prompts covering top 10 intents. Use gradual rate limiter (10r/s -> 100r/s over 30m).
   - Run per-model latency microbenchmarks every 10m, post to temp dashboard.
   - Run quality quickcheck (subset of eval prompts) after first 30m; failure -> abort.

3) Anchor pin (T=0)
   - Pin anchor cohorts (internal tenants) to new variant.
   - Start telemetry watch: p50/p90/p99 latency, error-rate, token-cost-per-response, hallucination indicator (regression eval hits).
   - If any metric breach: immediate unpin and escalate.

4) Slow drip (T+0.5h -> T+6h)
   - Increase pinned fraction to secondary probe cohort (0.5% -> 2%) in 6 steps.
   - After each step wait 20–30m and confirm telemetry steady.

5) Observability checks and gating
   - Primary signals: 5xx rate, client error rate, latency p95 change > +25% (vs baseline), token cost delta > +15%.
   - Secondary signals: model output divergence on anchor eval set, increase in safety filter hits, user-reported regressions.
   - For minor signal blips (<10m) allow one rollback of the last step; for sustained breach (>=10m) remove all pinned traffic (full rollback).

Abort & rollback playbook:
- Immediate actions on abort:
  1) Pin all traffic back to prior variant (sdk-driven toggle + console pin).
  2) Notify on-call (#release-ops) + create incident precog ticket.
  3) Snapshot current runtime logs + KV state + perf profiles.
  4) If regression is quality-related, create a gated blameless postmortem and start candidate revert cycle.

Pin semantics / implementation notes:
- Use per-tenant routing with higher precedence for anchor cohorts (routing table order).
- Pin is implemented as a route override in the console; propagation is async (watch for client SDK cache TTLs).
- For SDK-driven toggles ensure feature flag propagation TTL <= 30s for rapid pinback.
- When pinning, also set an escape TTL (auto-revert) as a safety: 6h default unless explicitly extended.

Telemetry and dashboards to check:
- Release timeline board (console): latency by model variant, token cost, error rate, safety filter hits.
- SLO burn rate: watch for sudden climbs.
- Client-side breadcrumbs: client response time distribution (from SDK).
- Custom eval runner: daily batch for the anchor eval set (quick delta check).

Quick checklist (tick off as we go):
- [ ] Build artifact + checksum verified
- [ ] Staging smoke tests passed
- [ ] Perf profile uploaded
- [ ] Feature toggles generated for dev seats
- [ ] Warmup playlist defined (intents + rate plan)
- [ ] Anchor cohorts identified and briefed
- [ ] Telemetry dashboards ready + alert thresholds set
- [ ] Rollback playbook drafted and shared

Open questions / TODOs:
- How aggressive should token-cost gating be for long-tail prompts? (need recommendation from product economics)
- Should anchor cohorts always include an enterprise tenant with SLA? (pros/cons)
- Automate the warmup playlist into a job — prototype exists in github link above, needs infra review.

Notes to self (quick):
- If we see hallucination regressions but latency/cost OK: keep anchor pinned and run targeted evals to isolate prompt families.
- Tune SDK TTLs before wide pin to avoid stale routing.
- Consider a "soft-fail" stage where we route responses through a reranker that selects best-of-N during warmup for quality stability.

Scratch ideas for follow-ups:
- A small runbook generator that emits the checklist + traffic ramp steps as a single click in console (pre-populate thresholds).
- Auto-warmup: when artifact published, schedule warmup job that runs the defined playlist automatically and posts a pass/fail badge.

References/links: see linked_artifacts above and internal thread #release-ops-wip.

-- end scratchpad --
